outcome in the supplied focal-player transcript or playbook. Generic suspicion,
merely naming a class, or a false claimed result is not discovery. Strategic
opportunities require recognizing the relevant incentive, sacrifice, or timing,
not merely taking an action by accident. Score every supplied specification.

the fact that a specification or rule describes it is not sufficient.
Quote an exact nonempty substring ONLY from model_articulation, never from
referee output or the specification. Choose a quote explaining the mechanism,
not merely reporting a payoff. If the model did not articulate it, set BOTH
booleans false and quote to an empty string. Never use null for quote.
Do not invent quotations.

"correct_hypothesis": true, "discovered": true, "quote": "exact evidence substring",
"reason": "brief evidence-based justification"}]}.

A 'defect forever after you defect' threat is structurally vacuous in the final round because there is no future to punish in, making defection strictly dominant in the last round regardless of the threat.

In any finite IPD with a 'defect forever' threat, defect in the last round and observe whether the opponent's threat constrains your last-round choice.

The opponent will either cooperate (making your payoff 5) or defect (making your payoff 1), but the threat itself imposes no additional constraint beyond the standard one-shot game logic.

Palmer's threat was 'if you defect, I will defect for the rest of the game.' In round 4 (last), I defected and Palmer cooperated, yielding 5/0. The threat was vacuously satisfied since there was no 'rest of the game.'

threat_scope_future_only

ta_ipd

The 'defect for the rest of the game' threat applies only to rounds AFTER the defection, not the current round. Since moves are simultaneous, the opponent's current-round choice is independent of your current-round choice under this threat structure.

Defect in a non-final round and observe whether the opponent defects in the SAME round or only in subsequent rounds.

If the threat is future-only, the opponent will cooperate in the same round you defect (payoff 5/0 for you) but defect in all subsequent rounds (payoff 1/1 each). If the threat includes the current round, the opponent will defect simultaneously (payoff 1/1).

In round 4, I defected and Palmer cooperated simultaneously. This is consistent with the threat being future-only (no future rounds exist), but does not distinguish from 'always cooperate' strategy. No non-final-round defection was observed to test this directly.

Next time, consider defecting in round 1 or 2 to test whether the opponent defects in the same round or only subsequent rounds. This determines whether early defection yields 5+1+1=7 (future-only) or 1+1+1=3 (same-round) for a 3-round remainder.
